questions.question: What does "HTML" stand for?
questions.hint: It's used to create web pages!
questions.explanation: HTML (HyperText Markup Language) is the standard language for creating web pages.

questions.question: Who invented the World Wide Web?
questions.explanation: Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web in 1989 while working at CERN.

questions.question: What does "AI" stand for?
questions.explanation: AI (Artificial Intelligence) refers to machines or programs that can perform tasks requiring human intelligence.

questions.question: How many bits are in a byte?
questions.hint: A byte is made up of this many bits.
questions.explanation: A byte consists of 8 bits. A bit is the smallest unit of data (0 or 1).

questions.question: What programming language is named after a type of coffee?
questions.explanation: Java is a programming language named after Java coffee, from the Indonesian island.

questions.question: What is 9 + 7?
What is 15 - 7?
questions.explanation: 15 - 7 = 8. Start at 15 and count back 7 steps.

questions.question: What is 4 × 5?
questions.explanation: 4 × 5 = 20. Four groups of five equals twenty.

questions.question: How many sides does a square have?
questions.hint: Count the corners too - same number!
questions.explanation: A square has 4 equal sides and 4 corners.

questions.question: What is 6 + 8?
questions.hint: Make 6 into 10 by taking 4 from the 8.
questions.explanation: 6 + 8 = 14. You can think of it as 10 + 4.

questions.question: What is 25 + 15?
What is 8 × 7?
questions.explanation: 8 × 7 = 56. This is an important multiplication fact.

questions.question: What is 72 ÷ 8?
questions.explanation: 72 ÷ 8 = 9. Division is the opposite of multiplication.

questions.question: What is 1/2 + 1/4?
What is the perimeter of a rectangle with length 5 and width 3?
questions.explanation: Perimeter = 2(length + width) = 2(5 + 3) = 2(8) = 16.

questions.question: What is 23 × 11?
questions.hint: Multiply by 10, then add the original number.
questions.explanation: 23 × 11 = 230 + 23 = 253. Quick trick for multiplying by 11!

questions.question: What is the value of 5² + 3²?
If x + 7 = 15, what is x?
What is 3/5 as a decimal?
questions.explanation: 3 ÷ 5 = 0.6. You can also think of it as 6/10.

questions.question: What is 15% of 200?
questions.hint: 10% of 200 is 20, so 15% is a bit more.

questions.question: What do bees make?
questions.hint: It's sweet and you can eat it!
questions.explanation: Bees collect nectar from flowers and turn it into honey.

questions.question: What color is the sky on a clear day?
questions.hint: Look up on a sunny day!
questions.explanation: The sky appears blue because of how sunlight scatters in the atmosphere.

questions.question: What do plants need to grow?
questions.hint: They need more than one thing!
questions.explanation: Plants need water, sunlight, air, and nutrients from soil to grow.

questions.question: How many legs does an ant have?
questions.hint: All insects have this many legs.
questions.explanation: Ants are insects, and all insects have 6 legs.

questions.question: What season comes after winter?
questions.hint: Flowers start to bloom in this season.
questions.explanation: Spring comes after winter, bringing warmer weather and new plant growth.

questions.question: What is the largest organ in the human body?
questions.explanation: Skin is the largest organ, protecting your body and helping regulate temperature.

questions.question: What gas do humans breathe out?
questions.hint: Plants need this gas for photosynthesis.
questions.explanation: We breathe in oxygen and breathe out carbon dioxide as a waste product.

questions.question: What is the center of the solar system?
questions.hint: All planets orbit around this star.
questions.explanation: The Sun is the star at the center of our solar system.

questions.question: What is the process by which water turns into vapor?
questions.hint: This happens when water gets hot.
questions.explanation: Evaporation is when liquid water turns into water vapor (gas).

questions.question: What type of rock is formed by cooling lava?
questions.explanation: Igneous rocks form when molten lava or magma cools and hardens.

questions.question: What is the most abundant gas in Earth's atmosphere?
questions.hint: It makes up about 78% of the air.
questions.explanation: Nitrogen makes up about 78% of Earth's atmosphere, oxygen is about 21%.

questions.question: What is the powerhouse of the cell?
questions.hint: It produces energy for the cell.
questions.explanation: Mitochondria generate most of the cell's energy in the form of ATP.

questions.question: At what temperature does water boil at sea level (in Celsius)?
questions.explanation: Water boils at 100°C (212°F) at sea level under standard atmospheric pressure.

questions.question: What force pulls objects toward the center of the Earth?
questions.explanation: Gravity is the force that attracts objects with mass toward each other.

questions.question: What is the chemical formula for table salt?
questions.explanation: Table salt is sodium chloride (NaCl), made of sodium and chlorine atoms.

questions.question: What country is the Great Wall located in?
questions.hint: It's in Asia and very long!
questions.explanation: The Great Wall of China is one of the world's largest structures.

questions.question: Who sailed across the ocean in 1492?
questions.explanation: Christopher Columbus sailed from Spain and reached the Americas in 1492.

questions.question: What is a pharaoh?
questions.explanation: Pharaohs were the kings of ancient Egypt.

questions.question: What did the ancient Romans build to carry water?
questions.explanation: Aqueducts were bridges that carried water to Roman cities.

questions.question: In what year did the Titanic sink?
questions.explanation: The RMS Titanic sank on April 15, 1912 after hitting an iceberg.

questions.question: Who wrote the Declaration of Independence?
questions.hint: He later became the 3rd US President.
questions.explanation: Thomas Jefferson was the primary author of the Declaration of Independence in 1776.

questions.question: What was the first civilization to develop writing?
questions.explanation: The Sumerians developed cuneiform writing around 3200 BCE in Mesopotamia.

questions.question: In what year did World War I begin?
questions.explanation: World War I began in 1914 and ended in 1918.

questions.question: Who was the first Emperor of Rome?
questions.explanation: Augustus (formerly Octavian) became the first Roman Emperor in 27 BCE.

questions.question: What ancient wonder was located in Alexandria, Egypt?
questions.hint: It helped ships navigate at night.
questions.explanation: The Lighthouse of Alexandria (Pharos) was one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.

questions.question: What is the opposite of "hot"?
questions.explanation: Cold is the opposite (antonym) of hot.

questions.question: How many vowels are in the English alphabet?
questions.explanation: The 5 vowels are A, E, I, O, and U.

questions.question: What do we call a word that sounds the same but has a different meaning?
questions.explanation: Homophones are words that sound alike but have different meanings and spellings.

questions.question: What is the plural of "child"?
questions.explanation: The plural of child is children, not childs.

questions.question: What punctuation mark shows strong emotion?
questions.explanation: An exclamation point (!) shows excitement, surprise, or strong emotion.

questions.question: What is a metaphor?
questions.explanation: A metaphor directly compares two things without using "like" or "as."

questions.question: What is an alliteration?
answers: Repetition of the same starting sound
questions.explanation: Alliteration is when words in a row start with the same sound.

questions.question: What does the prefix "bio-" mean?
questions.explanation: The prefix "bio-" means life (from Greek bios).

questions.question: What is a haiku?
questions.explanation: A haiku is a Japanese poem with 3 lines: 5 syllables, 7 syllables, 5 syllables.

questions.question: What is the subject of a sentence?
answers: Who or what the sentence is about
questions.hint: In "The cat ran," the subject is "the cat."
questions.explanation: The subject is who or what is doing the action in the sentence.

questions.question: What comes next: 1, 2, 3, 4, ...?
questions.explanation: This is counting by ones: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.

questions.question: If you have 3 apples and get 2 more, how many do you have?
questions.explanation: 3 + 2 = 5 apples.

questions.question: What shape has no corners?
questions.explanation: A circle has no corners or straight edges.

questions.question: If today is Monday, what day was yesterday?
questions.explanation: The day before Monday is Sunday.

questions.question: Which doesn't belong: dog, cat, tree, rabbit?
questions.explanation: Tree is a plant; the others are all animals.

questions.question: If 5 cats can catch 5 mice in 5 minutes, how many cats are needed to catch 100 mice in 100 minutes?
questions.explanation: Each cat catches 1 mouse per 5 minutes, so 5 cats can catch 100 mice in 100 minutes.

questions.question: What is the next number in the sequence: 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, ...?
questions.explanation: This is the Fibonacci sequence: each number is the sum of the two before it (5 + 8 = 13).

questions.question: If A = 1, B = 2, C = 3, what does "CAB" equal?
questions.hint: Replace each letter with its number.

questions.question: In a race, you pass the person in 2nd place. What place are you in now?
questions.explanation: If you pass the person in 2nd place, you are now in 2nd place.

questions.question: Which is heavier: a pound of feathers or a pound of rocks?
questions.explanation: They both weigh one pound, so they are equal in weight!

questions.question: What is the largest ocean on Earth?
questions.hint: It's between Asia and the Americas.
questions.explanation: The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean on Earth.

questions.question: What is the capital of France?
questions.explanation: Paris is the capital city of France.

questions.question: On which continent is the Amazon Rainforest?
questions.hint: It's in Brazil and nearby countries.
questions.explanation: The Amazon Rainforest is mostly in Brazil, South America.

questions.question: What is the longest river in the world?
questions.explanation: The Nile River in Africa is considered the longest river at about 6,650 km.

questions.question: How many continents are there?
questions.explanation: There are 7 continents: Africa, Antarctica, Asia, Europe, North America, Australia/Oceania, South America.

questions.question: What is the smallest country in the world?
questions.explanation: Vatican City is the smallest country, with an area of about 0.44 km².

questions.question: Which desert is the largest hot desert in the world?
questions.explanation: The Sahara Desert in Africa is the largest hot desert in the world.

questions.question: What is the tallest mountain in the world?
questions.explanation: Mount Everest is 8,849 meters (29,032 feet) tall, the highest point on Earth.

questions.question: Which country has the most people?
questions.explanation: India has the world's largest population as of 2024.

questions.question: What line divides the Earth into Northern and Southern hemispheres?
questions.explanation: The Equator is an imaginary line at 0° latitude that divides Earth into hemispheres.

questions.question: What is 11 + 9?
questions.explanation: 11 + 9 = 20. You can think of it as (10 + 10).

questions.question: What is 100 - 35?
What is 9 × 9?
questions.explanation: 9 × 9 = 81. This is an important multiplication fact.

questions.question: What is 50% of 80?
What is the area of a square with side length 6?
questions.explanation: Area of square = 6 × 6 = 36 square units.

questions.question: What do we call a baby dog?
questions.explanation: A baby dog is called a puppy.

questions.question: How many wings does a butterfly have?
questions.hint: Count them: two on each side.
questions.explanation: Butterflies have 4 wings - two on the left and two on the right.

questions.question: What is the fastest land animal?
questions.explanation: Cheetahs can run up to 70 mph, making them the fastest land animal.

questions.question: What is the main gas in the air we breathe?
questions.hint: It makes up about 78% of air.
questions.explanation: Nitrogen makes up about 78% of Earth's atmosphere.

questions.question: What do we call animals that eat only plants?
questions.explanation: Herbivores are animals that eat only plants (like deer, cows, and rabbits).

questions.question: What did people use before cars to travel?
questions.explanation: Before cars, people used horses and horse-drawn carriages for transportation.

questions.question: Who was the first president of the United States?
questions.hint: His face is on the $1 bill.
questions.explanation: George Washington was the first U.S. president (1789-1797).

questions.question: What was the name of the ship the Pilgrims sailed on?
questions.hint: It's also a type of flower.
questions.explanation: The Pilgrims sailed to America on the Mayflower in 1620.

questions.question: In which country did the Industrial Revolution begin?
questions.explanation: The Industrial Revolution began in England in the late 1700s.

questions.question: Who invented the light bulb?
questions.hint: He had a famous laboratory in Menlo Park.
questions.explanation: Thomas Edison invented the practical incandescent light bulb in 1879.

questions.question: What is a baby cat called?
questions.explanation: A baby cat is called a kitten.

questions.question: What do we call words that rhyme at the end of poem lines?
questions.explanation: When the last words of lines rhyme, it's called end rhyme.

questions.question: What is the superlative form of "good"?
questions.explanation: The superlative of good is best (not "most good" or "gooder").

questions.question: What is an oxymoron?
questions.explanation: An oxymoron combines contradictory terms (like "clearly confused").

questions.question: What do we call a word that is spelled the same backward and forward?
questions.explanation: A palindrome reads the same backward as forward.

questions.question: What comes next: red, blue, red, blue, ...?
questions.explanation: The pattern alternates: red, blue, red, blue, so red comes next.

questions.question: If all birds have wings, and a robin is a bird, what can we say?
answers: A robin is not a bird
questions.explanation: If all birds have wings, then a robin (which is a bird) must have wings.

questions.question: What number comes next: 3, 6, 9, 12, ...?
questions.explanation: This sequence adds 3 each time: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15.

questions.question: If you rearrange the letters in "LISTEN," what word do you get?
questions.hint: All the letters can make more than one word!
questions.explanation: LISTEN is an anagram of SILENT, ENLIST, and TINSEL.

questions.question: What is the missing number: 2, 4, 8, 16, ...?
questions.hint: Each number is double the previous one.
questions.explanation: This sequence doubles each time: 2, 4, 8, 16, 32.
